en: Anxiety or fear that something bad will happen; also, understanding or arrest
hook: APPREHENSION: feeling like you're about to be APPREHENDED (arrested).
story: Sara felt apprehension the night before her visa interview, imagining every possible question and every way it could go wrong. Apprehension means anxious fear about the future. It can also mean arrest, as in the apprehension of a thief, or understanding.

en: Very enthusiastic or passionate
hook: ARDENT: burning with ARDOR.
story: Arif is an ardent fan of Humayun Ahmed's novels; he has read every one at least three times and can quote whole pages. Ardent means passionately devoted. Synonyms: fervent, zealous, fervid.

en: Self-evident; accepted as true without proof
hook: AXIOM: a basic truth in math, needing no proof.
story: It is axiomatic that practice improves skill; nobody needs a study to prove it. In geometry, axioms are truths accepted without proof, like 'a straight line is the shortest distance between two points.' Axiomatic means self-evidently true.

en: To come to an end; to stop
hook: CEASE: CEASE-FIRE, stop shooting.
story: At exactly midnight, the guns ceased firing and the ceasefire began. Families came out of hiding for the first time in weeks. To cease is to stop. Incessant means never ceasing. Cease and desist means stop immediately.

en: Making a certain outcome likely; helpful
hook: CONDUCIVE: CONDUCTS you toward a result.
story: A quiet room, a comfortable chair, and good light are conducive to studying. Loud music and phone notifications are not. Conducive means creating good conditions for something. Warm, wet weather is conducive to rice growth.

en: Relating to the physical body; material rather than spiritual
hook: CORPOREAL: CORPS, CORPSE, body.
story: Ghosts in stories are not corporeal; they pass through walls because they have no physical body. The monk cared little for corporeal comforts like food and sleep. Corporeal means bodily or physical. Corporal punishment is physical punishment.

en: Rigidly applying a theory without regard for practical considerations
hook: DOCTRINAIRE: follows the DOCTRINE no matter what.
story: The doctrinaire economist insisted his theory must be applied exactly, even when the results were clearly hurting farmers. 'The theory cannot be wrong,' he said. Doctrinaire means rigidly devoted to a theory. Synonym: dogmatic.

en: Drawing from a wide variety of sources or styles
hook: ECLECTIC: ELECTS a bit from everywhere.
story: Mitu's playlist is eclectic: Rabindra Sangeet, K-pop, Arabic oud music, and heavy metal, all shuffled together. Eclectic means drawn from diverse sources. An eclectic decor mixes antique and modern furniture.

en: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficulty
hook: EQUA-NIMITY: an EQUAL, balanced mind.
story: When his flight was cancelled and his luggage lost, the old monk accepted the news with complete equanimity: 'Then I will wait.' Not a trace of anger. Equanimity means calm composure. Synonyms: serenity, poise, composure.

en: Unreasonably high, especially of price
hook: EX-ORBIT-ANT: prices gone OUT OF ORBIT.
story: The hotel near the airport charged an exorbitant price: five hundred taka for a cup of tea. Tanvir decided to wait outside. Exorbitant means unreasonably expensive. Synonyms: excessive, extortionate.

en: Changing frequently, especially in loyalty or affection
hook: FICKLE: FLICKERS like a candle.
story: Cricket fans can be fickle: heroes one day, villains the next after a single bad match. Rafi's little brother is fickle too; his favorite food changes every week. Fickle means changeable, especially in loyalty. Synonyms: capricious, mercurial.

en: Not literal; using figures of speech like metaphors
hook: FIGURATIVE: a FIGURE of speech.
story: When Nadia said she was 'dying of hunger,' her mother knew it was figurative, not literal. Figurative language uses words beyond their literal meaning: metaphors, similes, and hyperbole. 'Time is money' is figurative.

en: Agitated, nervous, and confused
hook: FLUSTERED: FLUSHED and FLUTTERED.
story: When the interviewer suddenly switched to French, Arif became flustered: he blushed, stammered, and forgot even his own address. Flustered means nervously confused. Synonyms: agitated, rattled, nonplussed.

en: Easily deceived or tricked
hook: GULLIBLE: like a sea GULL that swallows anything thrown at it.
story: 'Did you know the word gullible isn't in the dictionary?' Rafi asked. His gullible cousin immediately went to check. Gullible means easily fooled. Gullible people fall for scams. Synonyms: credulous, naive.

en: Peculiar to an individual; distinctive and unusual
hook: IDIO-SYNCRATIC: IDIO means one's own (as in idiom).
story: The professor had an idiosyncratic teaching style: he lectured while walking backwards, drew diagrams with his left hand, and ended every class with a poem. Idiosyncratic means peculiar to one person. An idiosyncrasy is a personal quirk.

en: Happening as a minor part or consequence of something more important
hook: INCIDENTAL: just a side INCIDENT.
story: The main cost of studying abroad is tuition; books, transport, and printing are incidental expenses. Incidental means minor, happening alongside something more important. Incidental music plays in the background of a film.

en: Firmly fixed or established, hard to change
hook: INGRAINED: deep IN the GRAIN of the wood.
story: The habit of waking at five was so ingrained in Grandpa that even on holidays he couldn't sleep past dawn. Ingrained means deeply fixed, like a stain in wood grain. Synonyms: entrenched, inveterate.

en: Boldly rude and disrespectful
hook: INSOLENT: INSULTING.
story: When the teacher asked for his homework, the student yawned and said, 'Why don't you do it yourself?' The class gasped at such an insolent reply. Insolent means rude and disrespectful. Synonyms: impertinent, impudent.

en: To mock or ridicule through satire
hook: LAMPOON: like a cartoon that LAMPS (lights up) someone's flaws for laughs.
story: The comedy show lampooned the city's mayor, showing him as a cartoon stuck in traffic while promising 'zero traffic jams.' To lampoon is to mock through satire. Political cartoonists lampoon leaders every day.

en: Rich, elaborate, and generous; to give generously
hook: LAVISH: like a LAVA flow of luxury.
story: The wedding reception was lavish: crystal chandeliers, ten kinds of meat, and gifts for every guest. Grandma lavished love on her grandchildren. Lavish means luxurious and abundant; to lavish is to give generously.

en: Looking or sounding sad and dismal
hook: LUGUBRIOUS: LUG-ubrious, LUGGING sadness around.
story: The old man's lugubrious face and slow, mournful voice made even a simple 'good morning' sound like a funeral announcement. Lugubrious means exaggeratedly mournful. Synonyms: morose, doleful, melancholy.

en: Disturbing and horrifying because involving death or injury
hook: MACABRE: think 'MAKE A BURIAL' scene.
story: The museum's exhibit of ancient skulls, torture tools, and mummies was macabre, fascinating some visitors and terrifying others. Macabre means gruesome and focused on death. Some horror movies have a macabre sense of humor.

en: Sullen and gloomy
hook: MOROSE: MORE OF A ROSE losing its petals, wilting sadly.
story: After losing his job, Tanvir became morose: he stayed in his room, barely spoke, and ignored his friends' calls. Morose means sullen and gloomy. Synonyms: lugubrious, glum, sullen.

en: Too eager to tell people what to do; intrusively interfering
hook: OFFICIOUS: acts like an OFFICER nobody appointed.
story: The officious neighbor told Mitu's family how to park, what to cook, and when to turn off their lights, though nobody ever asked him. Officious means intrusively bossy. Don't confuse it with official.

en: A complex consequence of an action or event
hook: RAMIFICATION: branches (rami) spreading out from a decision.
story: The decision to close the factory had ramifications across the town: shops lost customers, families moved away, and schools lost students. Ramifications are the consequences that branch out from an action. Synonym: repercussion.

en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled
hook: SERENE: SERENITY.
story: At sunrise, the lake in Rangamati was serene: still water, soft mist, and only the sound of a distant boat. Serene means calm and peaceful. A serene face shows inner peace. Synonyms: tranquil, placid.

en: To replace, especially by force or scheming
hook: SUP-PLANT: uproot one PLANT and put another in its place.
story: Online shopping has supplanted many neighborhood stores. In the palace drama, the ambitious minister plotted to supplant the king. To supplant is to take the place of someone or something, often by force. Synonym: supersede.

en: Understood or implied without being stated
hook: TACIT: TACITURN, silent agreement.
story: The roommates had a tacit agreement: whoever cooks doesn't wash the dishes. They never discussed it; it just worked. Tacit means understood without words. Tacit approval means silently accepting something.

en: To go beyond the limits of
hook: TRANS-CEND: climb (scend) ACROSS (trans) the limits.
story: Music transcends language. Bengali songs move listeners who don't understand a word. Great leaders transcend party politics. To transcend is to go beyond ordinary limits. Transcendent means surpassing ordinary experience.

en: A formal written work dealing systematically with a subject
hook: TREATISE: a book that TREATS a subject thoroughly.
story: The professor spent twenty years writing a five-hundred-page treatise on the history of Bengali music. A treatise is a formal, systematic written work on a subject. Newton's Principia is a famous treatise on physics.
